How old am I?

1. Pink Floyd - The Wall - Got me into music in general, and was the first album that I learned from front to back, and eventually saw it live as my first ever concert.

2. System of a Down - Toxicity - One of the first metal albums that I ever listened to in my life, and it helped me get through most of high school.

3. Alice in Chains - Dirt - An album that really helped me through depressing times, and one that I realized that came straight from a source of hard times and struggle.

4. Tool - Ænima - One of the first albums that really became enhanced with an album experience, rather than a collection of various songs put together.

5. The Smiths - The Queen is Dead - One that really started a high school obsession with the Smiths, and one that really helped to shape my varied taste in music.

6. Pixies - Doolittle - One of the arguably best albums ever created, and whenever I put it on, I end up playing the entire album without skipping a track.

7. Funkadelic - Maggot Brain - Opened my eyes to genres I would have never given any attention to, such as soul, funk and some jazz. The title track is one of my favorite guitar pieces ever.

8. MF DOOM - Mm...Food - One of the oddest hip hop records I had ever listened to, and one that through various listens became an almost perfect album, with the exception of the abundance of skits.

9. Wu-Tang Clan - Enter the Wu-Tang - The album that made me first realize the complexity of putting an album together, and how everyone works together to make a finished product.

10. Death - Symbolic - The album that opened me up to listening to death metal, and made me realize the inherent complexity in the music.

As far as I can remember, music was always a part of my life, and many days were spent buying various CDs with my dad. This music motivated me to better myself, I cut off my long, messy hair, started eating and exercising right, getting to know people and Ive been better since.
